Title: Document 4
Content: . . .From `1961` to `1971`, the U.S. military sprayed a range of herbicides across more than `text(4.5 million acres)` of Vietnam to destroy the forest cover and food crops used by enemy North Vietnamese and Viet Cong troops.

U.S. aircraft were deployed to douse [spray down] roads, rivers, canals, rice paddies and farmland with powerful mixtures of herbicides. During this process, crops and water sources used by the non-combatant native population of South Vietnam were also hit.

In all, American forces used more than `text(20 million gallons)` of herbicides in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia during the `text(years)` of Operation Ranch Hand. Herbicides were also sprayed from trucks and hand-sprayers around U.S. military bases. . . .
